en: A non-root dhamma that is visible and impinging is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a dhamma that is neither root nor visible nor impinging …pe… a non-root dhamma that is visible and impinging is a condition,
by way of object-condition, for both a dhamma that is neither root nor visible nor impinging and a dhamma that is neither root nor visible nor impinging.
Three [conditions] by way of object; three by way of predominance, decisive support, prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance.

In dependence on a state that is not-root and non-demonstrable-with-resistance, a state that is not-root and non-demonstrable-with-resistance arises by way of root-condition. One [condition] by way of root... pe ... one by way of non-disappearance.
In dependence on a state that is root and non-demonstrable-without-resistance, a state that is not-root and non-demonstrable-without-resistance arises.

By way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*). Dependent on a state that is not a root (*nahetu*) and non-demonstrable and non-reactive (*anidassana-appaṭigha*), there arises a state that is not a root and non-demonstrable and non-reactive by way of root condition.

Dependent on both a state that is a root and non-demonstrable and non-reactive, and a state that is not a root and non-demonstrable and non-reactive, there arises a state that is not a root and non-demonstrable and non-reactive by way of root condition. (3) Under root condition.
Three ... [and so on] ... three in the case of non-disappearance.
